subject: Analysing UK biobank raw accelerometer data using GGIR

messages.author: 1950870f8058d31e
messages.subject: Analysing UK biobank raw accelerometer data using GGIR
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to extract sleep measures from UK BioBank raw accelerometer data (AX3) using GGIR package (v2.1-0). I came across couple of papers and also some posts in this group, in which it is recommended to first convert .cwa files to .wav files using omconvert. I was wondering if anyone could advise what’s the reason behind this? As far as I looked into GGIR guideline, it can resample and auto-calibrate the input raw signal.

Also, I am new to sleep research and using the following script for analysing the AX3 data. I was wondering if anyone has any suggestions/experience for parameter setup on this dataset? Any input would be highly appreciated.

 

 g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------

             # General parameters

             #-------------------------------

             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5)

             datadir = "/UKBB/Raw_Data/",

             outputdir = “/UKBB/GGIR_output/”,

             overwrite = FALSE,

             do.parallel = T,

             chunksize = 1,

             idloc=2,

             storefolderstructure = FALSE,

             print.filename=TRUE,

             #=====================

             # Part 1

             #=====================

             printsummary=TRUE,

             #=====================

             # Part 2

             #=====================

             strategy = 1,

             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,

             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,

             qwindow=c(0,24),

             mvpathreshold =c(100),

             bout.metric = 4,

             excludefirstlast = FALSE,

             includenightcrit = 16,

             #=====================

             # Part 3 + 4

             #=====================

             def.noc.sleep = 1,

             outliers.only = FALSE,

             criterror = 4,

             do.visual = TRUE,

             #=====================

             # Part 5

             #=====================

             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),

             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,

             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),

             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),

             includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,

             timewindow = c("WW"),

             #=====================

             # Report generation

             #=====================

             #do.report=c(2, 3, 4, 5),

             dofirstpage = TRUE,

             visualreport=TRUE)

 

Kind regards,

Mahnoosh

messages.subject: Re: Analysing UK biobank raw accelerometer data using GGIR
parts:
Another question on analysing .wav files using GGIR:

I noticed that GGIR package takes very long (like forever,  > 4 hours) without neither any output nor an error! I just had a look at the first 16 lines of the .wav file header:

RIFF???WAVEfmt (??d??8?qLIST?INFOINAM?Session: 1179855220

ClearTime: 2106-02-07 06:28:15.000

ChangeTime: 2013-12-17 18:42:46.000

Start: 2013-12-20 10:00:00.000

Stop: 2013-12-27 10:00:00.000

Config-A: 100,8

Metadata: 

IART0Id: 2746

Device: CWA

Revision: 17

Firmware: 35

ICMTzTime: 2013-12-20 10:00:00.000

Channel-1: Accel-X

Scale-1: 8

Channel-2: Accel-Y

Scale-2: 8


It seems this header causes trouble in g.wavread function (stuck in a while loop). Just wondering if anyone else came across this problem before?

This is how I am converting a .cwa file to .wav format (with linear interpolation):

./omconvert /UKBB/Data/1000139_90001_0_0.cwa -interpolate-mode 2 -out 1000139_90001_0_0.wav -info 1000139_90001_0_0.yml


Thanks,

Mahnoosh

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Analysing UK biobank raw accelerometer data using GGIR
parts: "I am trying to extract sleep measures from UK BioBank raw accelerometer data (AX3) using GGIR package (v2.1-0). I came across couple of papers and also some posts in this group, in which it is recommended to first convert .cwa files to .wav files using omconvert. I was wondering if anyone could advise what’s the reason behind this? As far as I looked into GGIR guideline, it can resample and auto-calibrate the input raw signal."

I implemented wav-format compatibility around 2015-2016. Functionality to handle cwa data was added a few years later by Evgeny and in January 2020 I made further improvements to that. However, recently it was discovered that there might be a minor offset in the data for cwa when it comes from older AX3 devices used in UK Biobank. devices: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/369. I do not think this is a major issue, but it would be good if this was investigated and resolved.

I have not worked with the wav-format data since we introduced the cwa read functionality. I am happy to investigate and try to improve both cwa and wav-format compatibility as a paid consultancy. On the other hand, if anyone else wants to investigate this and make a pull request than that is also fine.

"Also, I am new to sleep research and using the following script for analyzing the AX3 data. I was wondering if anyone has any suggestions/experience for parameter setup on this dataset? Any input would be highly appreciated."

I believe Sam Jones shared his R scripts in supplementary file data 10 to our manuscript: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-09576-1 Best advise is probably to dive into the package documentation and familiarise yourself with all function arguments used. If you encounter any issue then let me know.

Best, 
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/
